scope: Stop-hook model relevance retrieval/turn/causal identity binding; source forensics only

atoms.what_it_does: Creates each retrieval_episodes row with retrieval_id, turn_id, episode_id, causal_id, session_id, generation and query_hash before later feedback.
atoms.why_it_exists: Round-scoped retrieval provenance and learning bookkeeping.
atoms.failure_mode: Identity exists durably but can be lost if downstream feedback locates the row indirectly.
atoms.concurrency_implication: Provides sufficient immutable row identity to avoid session-newest selection if propagated.

atoms.what_it_does: Creates a fresh causal_id plus round-scoped turn_id and episode_id for each UserPromptSubmit and passes all three with generation into MicroClay.retrieve.
atoms.why_it_exists: Repairs prior session-scoped uniqueness collapse and makes repeated retrieval rounds representable.
atoms.failure_mode: The generated round identity is not returned through the later Stop hook API, so downstream relevance credit does not consume it directly.
atoms.concurrency_implication: Distinct same-session retrieval rounds are intentionally possible.
known_counterevidence: Source comment reports an earlier live uniqueness failure before this repair; current runtime state not re-observed in this trigger.

atoms.what_it_does: Receives only session_id and transcript_path, selects the newest same-session retrieval lacking modell:relevanz feedback, separately reads the last user message from the transcript, obtains a model judgment, then applies credit to the selected row.
atoms.why_it_exists: Adds model-derived relevance feedback while keeping the model from writing unified.db directly.
atoms.failure_mode: Target row and query are resolved independently at Stop time; under overlap/reordering they can belong to different turns even though both have stronger identities available upstream.
atoms.concurrency_implication: Same-session interleaving can plausibly misattach model relevance unless exact retrieval/turn identity is carried end-to-end.
atoms.privacy_implication: Candidate memory text plus last user query is sent to configured Ollama endpoint; endpoint locality is separately unresolved by prior delta.
atoms.latency_or_cost_implication: Synchronous model call remains inside Stop critical path; covered by prior Stop-hook boundary delta.
atoms.state_lifetime: request computation plus durable reduced feedback
known_counterevidence: No runtime wrong-row attachment observed yet.
open_questions: Can two same-session Stop events reorder on the installed host?
Does transcript last-user resolution ever diverge from the selected retrieval row under real hook scheduling?

atoms.what_it_does: Invokes _kognition_richten_hook from Stop with session_id and transcript_path only; no retrieval_id, turn_id, episode_id, causal_id or generation is passed.
outputs: call to relevance cognition then later Stop bookkeeping
atoms.failure_mode: Causal identity created at UserPromptSubmit is not preserved across the hook boundary.
atoms.concurrency_implication: Forces downstream re-discovery by session ordering instead of exact causal binding.
atoms.latency_or_cost_implication: Also places cognition before later Stop bookkeeping; prior delta covers timing risk.

hypotheses: The core retrieval-feedback identity defect is not missing identity in UnifiedDB; it is loss of already-created round identity across the UserPromptSubmit->Stop cognition boundary.
A typed RetrievalRelevanceCandidate bound to retrieval_id+turn_id+episode_id+causal_id+generation+query_hash can remove session-order dependence without changing canonical truth authority.
counterhypotheses: Claude hook scheduling may serialize UserPromptSubmit and Stop strongly enough that newest-open selection is operationally safe in the installed runtime; source alone cannot establish or refute this.
Even with exact retrieval_id, using transcript-derived last-user text could still mismatch unless the job carries the exact query or a query digest/value reference from retrieval creation.
contradictions: The donor deliberately creates fresh round-scoped causal/turn/episode identities for repeated same-session retrieval, but the later model-feedback hook does not consume those identities and instead falls back to session-newest discovery.
critical_unknowns: Installed hook ordering/concurrency under two same-session retrieval rounds.
Whether transcript last-user text and retrieval_episodes.query_hash remain aligned under reordered Stop processing.
Exact runtime behavior after a slow or timed-out first Stop overlaps a later turn.

recommended_next_spans.reason: Cross-check event-wide timeout transfer semantics against identity handoff and skipped later bookkeeping.
Use retrieval receipt/row identity as the source for a typed candidate contract; inspect whether query_hash plus selected_memory_ids are sufficient for replay-safe relevance work.
